title: Dengue admissions jump to 2,260 in a day; deaths reach 466
excerpt: Admissions rose by more than a third in 48 hours, and over 6,000 people are now in hospital with dengue.
content:
At least five people died of dengue and 2,260 were admitted to hospital in the 24 hours to 8am on Monday, 9 November, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), The Daily Star and Views Bangladesh reported.

The numbers

  • Deaths this year: 466. Three of the latest deaths were in Dhaka division, one in Mymensingh and one in Barishal.
  • Admissions this year: 152,173, of whom 145,593 have recovered and 6,114 are still in hospital.
  • Trend: on 7 November, DGHS reported 1,674 admissions in 24 hours. The 9 November figure of 2,260 is about 35% higher.

Why it matters

Health experts had warned the outbreak would not ease before December, and the jump in admissions supports that. More than 6,000 people in hospital at once puts pressure on district hospitals that are also treating children in the measles outbreak. NGOs running community health, WASH and urban programmes can support clean-ups of breeding sites and early referral, especially outside Dhaka.

What to watch

Whether daily admissions keep rising this week, and whether DGHS reports a new single-day high.
